verdicts.misleading_risk: Low for the site, but the report overstates the problem. CLS 0.100 on app pages sits exactly on the 'good' threshold. The figure is 0.100 on /apps/celltrackscolab/, /apps/nucleisky/ and /apps/labconstrictor-demo/, which I measured on Linux, so the Mac figure of 0.126 was not re-tested. The 0.159 figures for /apps/nucleisky/ and vlab4mic are not reproduced: /apps/nucleisky/ measured 0.100 with no header shift in that run, so those totals mix the header shift in only on cold loads. The proposed 'visibility:hidden box plus noscript style with !important' also adds a hidden dead box and a second mechanism where a simpler one exists. Moving the tile with a head script that duplicates the OS sniffing from lc.js would create a second place that decides the user's system.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
Fix the three shifts with CSS and one tiny head line, without duplicating OS detection:
(1) Header. Reserve the search slot: in lc.css give .lc-header__tools a fixed min-width and min-height of 1.76rem, and show .md-search__button always, with `.no-js .lc-header .md-search__button{visibility:hidden}`. Material puts class no-js on <html> (verified) and removes it in bundle.js, so no extra script is needed. The header then stays 72 px before and after JS and the menu no longer moves. This is the only fix that matters for the home page (0.330 measured on a cold load, 0.026 warm).
(2) Filter. Keep `hidden` in pages_apps.py:25 for no-JS. Add one inline line to overrides/main.html extrahead, `document.documentElement.classList.add('lc-js')`, and CSS `.lc-js .lc-filter[hidden]{display:flex}`. Also give .lc-filter__count a min-height, because its text appears after wiring and would shift the grid again (the area-based CLS is the same size). This avoids !important, invisible boxes and noscript blocks.
(3) OS tiles. Do not move DOM nodes at all. Keep the tile in its place in the grid and mark it in place (is-yours border plus 'Your system' label already exist), and on a Mac swap the ghost/filled classes in place (drop h3.after(mine), lc.js:43). This is the smallest change, adds no sniffing code in <head>, and keeps 'every tile stays visible'. If the team wants 'yours first', accept 0.1 on app pages; do not add a second UA-sniffing script.
Re-measure on cold and warm loads, desktop only, with the same observer. Target is below 0.05 on every page type. Do not split lc.css for this change (the 300-line rule is enforced for Python only, tests/test_code_rules.py:9).
verdicts.evidence: I measured with Playwright (Chromium 1194, 1280x800, no throttling). Cold home page: 0.330, one shift of 0.33 (sources lc-menu, md-container). Warm home page: 0.026 (comic). /apps/: 0.099, one DIV (filter). /apps/celltrackscolab/, /apps/nucleisky/ and /apps/labconstrictor-demo/: 0.100 from lc-ostile (/apps/labconstrictor-demo/ also 0.005 from lc-menu). Header height measured 67 px with JS disabled and 72.1875 px with JS on. Page source: `<html lang="en" class="no-js">` and bundle.js contains classList.remove("no-js"). Code: lc.js:36 grid.prepend(tile), lc.js:43 tile.querySelector("h3").after(mine), lc.js:79 form.hidden = false, pages_apps.py:25 `hidden`. DESIGN.md has no rule that the visitor's tile must be first (grep found none). Phone width (390): /apps/ measured 0.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low, but sub-claims (c) and (d) are weaker than stated. (c) Both focus styles are clearly visible (#1c5f1c on white is about 7:1, #10211a on white is higher), so this is a cosmetic inconsistency, not a WCAG failure. Forcing one style with `[dir] .md-typeset :focus-visible` fights Material's specificity and risks breaking its code-copy and search focus styles. (d) The phantom div is only verified in headless Chromium: it has tabIndex -1 and no tabindex attribute, and it became document.activeElement four times in a row on /apps/nucleisky/ (stops 44 to 47) before focus returned to BODY. That looks like the focus-wrap behaviour of a headless browser plus the js-focus-visible polyfill, not a real keyboard stop. Fixing it blind would be an unverified patch.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
Build only the two verified fixes in lc.css, about 2 lines:
(a) `.md-skip:focus{z-index:30}` (the header is z-index 20, lc.css:50; Material's skip link is 10). Then check the screenshot that the link is visible over the header at 1280 and 390 px.
(b) `.lc-footer :focus-visible{outline-color:#fff}`. White on #0f2214 is 16.7:1; the current #1c5f1c is 2.15:1.
Do not force one global outline. Instead change the DESIGN.md sentence to 'one visible outline colour for all links, a white one in the footer', or leave the sentence as is, because the actual difference is only colour and offset. Drop (d) unless someone reproduces an extra stop in headed Chrome, Firefox or Safari. Do not add display:none on an unknown Material element. Add the tab-walk check as a one-off script, not a repo test.
verdicts.evidence: On /apps/ at 1280 px, after the first Tab: activeElement is a.md-skip with text 'Skip to content', z-index 10, box (10,18,111x27); elementFromPoint at its centre returns IMG (the brand logo). The screenshot skip.png of the top 120 px shows only the header with no skip link. Footer links on /apps/: computed outline 2px solid rgb(28,95,28) on all 10 footer stops. Contrast computed: #1c5f1c on #0f2214 = 2.15, white on #0f2214 = 16.68. lc.css:40 `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--lc-accent-strong); outline-offset: 3px; }`. Built Material CSS has `.md-typeset a.focus-visible{outline-color:var(--md-accent-fg-color);outline-offset:.2rem}`, so content links use a different ring. The fixed div: `<div style="position: fixed; height: 100%; top: 0px; z-index: 4;">`, tabIndex -1, parent BODY; it only gets class focus-visible once activeElement lands on it.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low. Two numbers in the proposal need correcting. #767f79 gives 3.84:1 on the #f3f8f1 filter band (about 4.1:1 on white), not 'at least 4.5:1'; that passes the 1.4.11 limit of 3:1 but is not 4.5. The monogram icons are aria-hidden and sit beside the app name, and the letter is 21.6px/600, which is not 'large text' (needs bold 700), so (c) is a design choice rather than a clear failure.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
Two one-line changes in lc.css, using existing tokens so no new colour is invented:
(a) `.lc-card__title small{opacity:1}` after line 151. That gives the 5.71:1 the stylesheet already intends (#5b6a61). Check whether other `small`, `.md-typeset` or opacity rules reduce a muted colour elsewhere, with one computed-style scan over the built pages.
(b) In lc.css:166 change `border:1px solid #cfcfcf` to `border:1px solid var(--lc-muted)` (5.7:1 on white, about 5.2:1 on the band). This is a token the site already uses, so there is no new grey.
(c) Optional, leave to design: start the monogram gradient at var(--lc-accent-strong) instead of --lc-accent, or leave it as decorative.
Skip the proposed offline contrast checker (the 'see T6' reference). It is a new tool to maintain for a small site; re-run the one computed-style scan before releases instead.
verdicts.evidence: Computed in Chromium on /apps/: `.lc-card__title small` colour rgb(91,106,97) with opacity 0.75, which composites to about rgb(132,143,137) on white, 3.3:1. lc.css:151 sets `color: var(--lc-muted)` and no opacity. The filter form is display:flex after JS. lc.css:166 uses `border: 1px solid #cfcfcf`. Computed contrast: #cfcfcf on white 1.56, on #f3f8f1 1.45, #767f79 on #f3f8f1 3.84, white on #1fb221 2.82, #5b6a61 on white 5.71.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Moderate, mostly from the performance claims. The LCP figures (3.04 s, 2.96 s, 3.37 s) come from throttled runs without gzip, so they are overstated, and the auditor says so; they should not go into the report as findings. The claim 'search.json fetched on every page including phones' is Material's default behaviour, not an error to fix. The font preload is speculative: no measurement shows it helps. Converting comic.png is unmeasured optimisation. Adding an author-controlled alt field to the manifest schema plus the initialiser form is heavy for one image. /guides/install/ measured 0.009 in a fresh context (claimed 0.193 on desktop; not reproduced), while /guides/notebook-usage/ 0.266 is reproduced.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
Do the verified, cheap, rule-fixing parts only:
(1) Eager loading. Home hero logo (340x340 at y=229, loading="lazy", the first visible content image): loading="eager" plus fetchpriority="high", which DESIGN.md Images already requires. First hub card image: eager in hubs.py:48 (pass a flag for the first one). Everything else stays lazy.
(2) Dimensions. Write width and height for the screenshot in pages_apps.py:203 and for the comic in pages_site.py:24, reading them with Pillow (already imported in images.py and hubs.py). For imported guide images, add width and height in finish_site.py (50 lines, build-time, offline) for local files under assets/docs-img; skip remote shields.io badges, whose size cannot be read offline (3 of the 28). This fixes the reproduced 0.266 on /guides/notebook-usage/ and the 0.026 comic shift.
(3) Screenshot alt. Amend DESIGN.md line 54 to say 'the caption is the description of a screenshot' to match check_design.py:27 (lc-shot__img whitelisted because a figcaption exists). Do not add an alt field to the schema; that is author-controlled and a single screenshot does not justify it.
Drop: font preload, comic format conversion, search.json, CSS render-blocking, until measured with gzip on. If the team wants LCP numbers, rerun with a gzip-capable server first.
